record.paper_title: Open Problems in Global Analysis. Structured Foliations and the Information Geometry
record.original_question: Given a finite-dimensional Lie group G, determine whether G admits a two-sided invariant Riemannian structure.

evidence.quote: Two-sided invariant Riemannian structure in a ﬁnite dimensional Lie Group G

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $G$ be a finite-dimensional (connected) Lie group. A Riemannian metric $g$ on $G$ is called two-sided invariant (or bi-invariant) if both left translations $L_a: G \to G$, $x \mapsto ax$, and right translations $R_a: G \to G$, $x \mapsto xa$, are isometries of $(G,g)$ for every $a \in G$. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on $G$ for the existence of a two-sided invariant Riemannian metric, and in that case describe the structure of $G$.
artifact.status_search_result: The existence problem for bi-invariant Riemannian metrics on finite-dimensional connected Lie groups is classical and solved. A connected Lie group admits a two-sided (bi-)invariant Riemannian metric if and only if it is isomorphic to the direct product of a compact Lie group and a vector group $\mathbb{R}^n$; equivalently, its Lie algebra is a direct sum of a compact (i.e. admitting an Ad-invariant positive definite inner product) semisimple ideal and an abelian ideal. This characterization is standard (Milnor, and many textbooks on Lie groups and Riemannian geometry).

status_evidence.title: Lie Groups with Bi-invariant Metrics (Bettiol notes)
status_evidence.snippet: A connected Lie group admits a bi-invariant metric iff it is isomorphic to the product of a compact group and a vector space.
status_evidence.claim: Standard characterization of Lie groups admitting bi-invariant Riemannian metrics.

status_evidence.title: Lie groups with bi-invariant Riemannian metric (CUHK)
status_evidence.snippet: Connected Lie groups admitting bi-invariant Riemannian metrics are direct products of compact semisimple Lie groups and abelian vector groups.
